tags.name: Account
tags.description: The signed-in user, organisations and entitlements.

tags.name: Screens
tags.description: Physical displays and their links to sites and devices.

tags.name: Plays
tags.description: Plays with trust score, band and phase, and the evidence events matched into each play.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Webhook endpoints Vojo delivers events to, their signing secrets (shown once per create, and on an idempotent replay of that create) and delivery history. Requires `developer_access`. For wrapper-verified plays subscribe to `verification.ping` (fires once a play has both content start and finish), `verification.score.preliminary` (the play's score at that same moment, before it settles) and `verification.score.final` (fires when a play's score is final and passes the endpoint's filter policy; `verification.score` is its deprecated alias). Subscribing to the final score through /v1 creates a permissive filter policy automatically (no minimum band, no event minimums), so it fires for every play in the endpoint's scope that becomes final after the subscription; score filters are not configurable in /v1 yet. A /v1 final-score subscription never replays past plays.

tags.name: Stats
tags.description: Aggregate reads (aggregate): one request per dashboard widget. Every play count is a count of plays, the same unit `GET /v1/plays` lists, so totals always reconcile with the play list.

tags.name: Test helpers
tags.description:
Integrator sandboxes only: call with a sandbox's test key (`vojo_test_…`),
which reaches only its own sandbox. A live key gets `403 test_mode_only`. Run a play with a chosen scenario on a simulated screen, and switch
background (ambient) plays on or off. A test play goes through the real
pipeline: its evidence is sent the way a real Passport and Harvester send
theirs, the real matcher opens the play and the real scorer settles it, so
the play, its events and its webhooks are exactly what live produces.

get.description:
Returns the signed-in user, their capabilities and — when
`Vojo-Organisation` is sent — their effective permissions in that org. OAuth only (secret keys have no user). Not subject to the operator gate.

put.description:
Persists `User.organisationId` (the org a fresh sign-in lands in). A target the user cannot access returns
403 `organisation_access_denied`. OAuth only; no org header needed.

get.description:
Cross-org read: every org the user is a member of or holds an access
grant to (and that is granted to this OAuth client), sorted by name. Small bounded set — not paginated. OAuth only; no org header.

post.description:
Creates an organisation owned by the user in one transaction (Organisation,
backing Client, an OWNER `OrganisationAccess` grant, optional Address) and
makes it the user's default org. A duplicate name returns 409
`duplicate_name`. OAuth only; no org header.

get.description:
The organisation this request acts on (the `Vojo-Organisation` header, or
the secret key's bound org). Lets a key holder confirm which org it is bound
to. Any valid token or key may call it — no specific scope is required.

Feature entitlements for the active org, with quantity limits and usage, so
a client can show upsell before hitting a 402. The API enforces
entitlements itself (e.g. `POST /v1/dashboards`). Small bounded set — not
paginated.

Screens in the org with the embedded site, harvester and size range. Vojo reports facts, not a screen status: `last_evidence_at` is when Vojo
last saw Passport or Harvester evidence. Cursor-paginated (max 100 per
page; page through with `next_cursor` to load a whole network). The
dashboard "recent evidence" view is `?sort=-last_evidence_at&limit=6`.

parameters.name: has_harvester
parameters.description: True = a harvester is paired; false = none. A screen does not need one.

post.description:
Creates a screen. `site_id` and `harvester_id` (optional) must belong to
the org and the harvester must be unassigned (409
`harvester_already_assigned`). A duplicate name returns 409
`duplicate_name`. Send `screen_size_range_id`, or `size_inches` and let the
server pick the band.

Linking fields need the same permission as their own sub-resource, in
addition to `networkAddNew`: sending `site_id` also requires
`sitesAssignScreen` (as `PUT /v1/screens/{screen_id}/site`), and sending
`harvester_id` also requires `networkUpdateHarvester` (as
`PUT /v1/screens/{screen_id}/harvester`). Without it the request fails
with 403 `permission_denied` and nothing is created.

get.description: One screen. Poll `last_evidence_at` to see when evidence last arrived. Another org's id returns 404.

patch.description:
Partial update of detail fields (JSON Merge Patch semantics). Site and
harvester links are separate sub-resources. A name clash returns
409 `duplicate_name`.

delete.description: Deletes the screen. Paired devices are detached, not deleted.

put.summary: Assign a harvester to a screen
put.description:
Pairs a harvester the org already owns to this screen. The harvester is
atomically detached from any other screen in the org. Re-assigning the
harvester already on this screen is a no-op (safe to retry). If this screen
has a different harvester, returns 409 `screen_already_paired` — unassign
it first. Not an activation path: use `POST /v1/harvesters` for a new device.

delete.description:
Detaches the harvester. The harvester, its id and calibration history are
kept, so it can be assigned again. 404 when the screen has no harvester.

put.summary: Assign a screen to a site
put.description: Sets the screen's site. The site must belong to the org.

delete.summary: Remove a screen from its site
delete.description: Clears the screen's site. 404 when the screen has no site.

post.description:
Captures a new quality baseline from the screen's latest scored quality
window (the same window the `screen.quality` webhook reports). With no
window yet, returns 409 `no_quality_readings`.

get.description:
Global reference data (not org-specific), sorted by `min_inches`. Small
fixed set — not paginated.

Zero-filled play counts per bucket plus the total, in scope. One call per
stat widget.

Screens whose paired harvester is offline or reports a quality problem,
ranked server-side. Harvester facts only — Vojo never assumes a screen's
own state, and a screen without a harvester never appears here. Returns ids, not links.

Read-only roll-up of current harvester issues (harvesters down at a site,
harvester quality on a screen), critical first. Harvester facts only —
never a screen on/off state. Small bounded set — not paginated. Requires the operator gate (`canViewOrgIssues`).

Per-site screen count and harvester online/total counts, with
coordinates, plus an `is_unassigned` bucket for devices with no site. Screens are counted, never classed online or offline. Bounded by the
org's site count — not paginated.

All-time and daily verified-play counts for one method. Org scope counts
every verification for the org (including Passport plays on non-Vojo
screens); `site` / `screen` scopes only count verifications with a screen.

Plays and stability per bucket, uptime and overall stability for one
screen. An unowned screen returns 404.

What played on the screen: detected fingerprints, linked advertisements,
play share, and a timeline of the top advertisements.

Per-channel colour and brightness scores against the latest baseline,
from the scored quality windows harvester-ingest records. These are the
same numbers the `screen.quality` webhook sends.
Verified plays per fingerprint per bucket for one harvester.

The Vojo-managed global HOME template (published). 404 tells the client to
use its built-in fallback. OAuth only — dashboards belong to users.

The caller's own dashboards plus the org's `organisation`-visibility
dashboards (the HOME template is excluded). OAuth only.

post.description:
Creates a dashboard owned by the caller in the active org (owner and org
come from the principal, never the body). Widgets are validated against the
widget catalog. Over the `dashboards.author` entitlement returns 402
`entitlement_limit_reached`. OAuth only.

get.description: One dashboard the caller can see, with widgets and `can_edit`. OAuth only.

patch.description:
Owner only. A dashboard the caller does not own, or the HOME template,
returns 404. OAuth only.

delete.description: Owner only. Idempotent: a missing or non-owned id also returns 204. OAuth only.

get.description:
Harvesters owned by the org. `assigned=false` lists those free to pair
(the screen form's picker).

parameters.name: assigned
parameters.description: True = paired to a screen; false = unassigned.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search by MAC address or description.

post.description:
Claims an unclaimed harvester for the org by its activation code, and
optionally pairs it to a screen. To move a harvester the org already owns,
use `PUT /v1/screens/{screen_id}/harvester`.

Sending `screen_id` pairs the harvester to that screen, so it also
requires `harvesterAssignScreen` (the flag the portal's harvester-side
assign-to-screen and install-setup flows check), in addition to
`harvesterInstall`. Without it the request fails with 403
`permission_denied` and the harvester is not claimed.

get.description: One harvester.
Sites in the org, sorted by name. Supports `q` typeahead (dashboard scope picker).

post.description:
Creates a site with optional address, coordinates and multi-range
operating times.

get.description: One site.

patch.description:
Partial update (JSON Merge Patch semantics). `operating_times` replaces
the whole week when sent.

delete.description: Deletes the site. Its screens are unassigned (not deleted).

post.description:
Generates proof-of-display wrapper HTML for a creative. `inline` returns
the HTML in `data.html`; `archive` stores it and returns `data.url`.

**The Passport always starts itself.** Wrappers created through this API
begin reporting as soon as the creative is shown and never wait for a
signal from the player, so verification stays independent of the
player. There is no option to change this.

**Two outcomes — handle both.** `201` means the wrapper is ready in the
response (e.g. this content was wrapped before). `202` means wrapping
continues in the background: the body carries the wrapper `id` with
`status: processing`; poll `GET /v1/wrappers/{wrapper_id}` (honour
`Retry-After`) or subscribe to the `wrapper.ready` / `wrapper.failed`
webhooks. Early implementations may always return `201`; do not rely on it. Requesting `fingerprint: true` additionally needs `advertisementFingerprinting`. Wrapper *delivery* is a separate process and not part of this contract.

202.description: Accepted — wrapping continues in the background.

Location.description: URL of the wrapper resource to poll.

Retry-After.description: Suggested seconds before the first poll.

get.description:
Returns a wrapper and its `status`. Use it to poll a wrapper that
`POST /v1/wrappers` returned with `202` until it is `ready` or `failed`.
Advertiser clients in the org, sorted by name.
One client.

Campaigns in the org. Read-only in v1. Supports `q` typeahead (dashboard
scope picker and `scope_type=campaign`).
One campaign, including `total_plays_on_target`.

Advertisements in the org. Archived ads are hidden by default; list them
with `is_active=false`.

post.description:
Step 2 of 2. Registers an uploaded object as an advertisement. The server
reads the object's size from storage — never from the client. A missing,
foreign or mismatched upload returns 422 (`upload_not_found` /
`upload_mismatch`). Setting `client_id` additionally needs
`advertisementAssignClients`.

Step 1 of 2. Reserves storage and returns a presigned PUT URL with
Content-Length and Content-Type signed in, so the PUT must match the
declared `size_bytes` and `content_type`. The object key is chosen by the
server. Over 2 GB returns 413; over the org's storage quota returns 402
`storage_quota_exceeded`. Then `POST /v1/advertisements` with the `upload_id`.

get.description:
One advertisement (archived ones included). `source_url` is populated only
for callers with `advertisementViewSource`.

delete.description:
Archives the advertisement: sets `is_active=false`. It disappears from
default lists and cannot be scheduled, but stays readable by id and
listable with `?is_active=false`. Proof-of-play is untouched and the media
is kept (it still counts toward the storage quota). Hard delete is not
available through the API. Idempotent.

get.description:
How plays were evidenced by Vojo's two sources, month by month: corroborated
(Passport and Harvester), Passport only, Harvester only, or neither. Aggregated
server-side over every play in range, never sampled. Months are UTC calendar
months of the play's start; months with no plays are returned as zeros.

parameters.name: months
parameters.description: How many months back, including the current month.

get.description:
Plays in the organisation, newest first. One play is one
play: the unit every play count in this API is built
from. Each play carries its per-track evidence status and its trust
score, band and phase (never the internal score breakdown). The
underlying evidence events are at `GET /v1/plays/{play_id}/events`.

parameters.name: external_id
parameters.description: The partner's own creative reference (for creatives never uploaded to Vojo).

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Narrows an `external_id` lookup to one partner namespace. Ignored without `external_id`.

parameters.name: band
parameters.description: Only plays whose current band is at least this (e.g. `high` returns high and max).

get.description: A single play with its track statuses and trust score.

The verification events matched into this play: Passport lifecycle events and harvester fingerprint reads. Oldest first. Partner echo fields are returned verbatim and are
never scored.
The organisation's webhook endpoints. Signing secrets are never returned here.

post.description:
Registers a URL to receive the selected events. The response includes the
endpoint's signing `secret`, shown once per create (and on an idempotent
replay of that create); no other read returns it (roll it to get a new
one). Verify deliveries with the `X-Vojo-Signature` header.

Idempotent replay: repeating this request with the same
`Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours returns the original 201 response,
including the original `secret`, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The
replay returns that original secret even if it has since been rolled or
the endpoint deleted. The stored response keeps the secret encrypted at
rest, never in plaintext.

Subscribing to `verification.score.final` (or its deprecated alias
`verification.score`): the endpoint is automatically given
a permissive filter policy: no minimum band, no event minimums, backfill
off. The event then fires for every play in the endpoint's scope that
reaches its final score after the subscription is made, and never for
plays that were already final (past plays are never replayed). `attestConfigId` in the event payload is the id of this filter policy. Score filters are not configurable through /v1 yet; they may
be added later as an additive change.

patch.description:
Change its name, URL, events, or enable/disable it. Does not change the secret.

Adding `verification.score.final` (or the `verification.score` alias)
to `enabled_events` gives the endpoint the
same permissive filter policy `createWebhookEndpoint` creates (no minimum band, no event minimums, backfill off), unless it already has one,
which is kept unchanged. The event fires only for plays in the
endpoint's scope that reach their final score after that filter policy is created; past plays are never replayed. `attestConfigId` in the payload
refers to that filter policy. Score filters are not configurable through /v1
yet.

delete.description: Stops all deliveries to this endpoint and deletes it.

post.summary: Roll a webhook endpoint's signing secret
post.description:
Issues a new signing secret, returned **once**. For `overlap_hours`
(default 24, max 168) the previous secret stays valid and deliveries
carry signatures from both the new and the previous secret, so receivers
can switch without dropping events: `X-Vojo-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<new>,v1=<previous>`. Receivers accept a
delivery if any `v1` matches any secret they hold. `overlap_hours: 0`
ends the previous secret immediately. it goes straight to signed with
the new secret. A roll inside a live overlap keeps the original previous
secret and extends the overlap to the later of the two end times, never
shortening it (the secret in between stops at once), so to roll twice on
purpose, wait for the overlap to end or send `overlap_hours: 0`. A portal
roll has no overlap.

get.description: Recent events sent (or queued) to this endpoint, newest first, with their latest attempt.

post.description: Queues the event for immediate redelivery. Returns 409 if it is already pending or succeeded.

Runs one simulated play now on a simulated screen in this sandbox,
showing `advertisement_id`, with the evidence `scenario` describes. Returns at once with a `test_play` (`status: queued`). The play
itself starts about a minute later (so the screen's sensor is heard
before it) and its evidence goes out over the following two minutes;
`play_id` fills in once the real matcher has opened the play. Poll `GET /v1/test_helpers/plays/{test_play_id}`
(honour `Retry-After`), or listen for the play's own webhooks.

Scenarios and the score each settles at (trust-score@4):

| scenario | evidence | settles at |
|---|---|---|
| `verified` | full Passport lifecycle + glass read | 100 |
| `partial` | Passport start + glass read | 85 |
| `glass_only` | glass read only | 75 |
| `passport_only` | full Passport lifecycle, sensor offline | 70 |
| `passport_start_only` | Passport start, sensor offline | 45 |
| `contradicted` | full lifecycle, glass reads another creative | 20 |
| `screen_off` | full lifecycle, sensor reports the screen off | 20 |
| `no_evidence` | nothing | no play (`play_id` stays null) |

`contradicted` needs a second creative in the sandbox. A play counts
towards the sandbox's daily simulated-play limit.

202.description: Accepted — the play's evidence goes out in the background.

Location.description: URL of the test play to poll.

Retry-After.description: Suggested seconds before the first poll.

get.description:
A test play and how far it has got: `queued` (accepted), `sending`
(its evidence is going out), `sent` (all of it has gone; the pipeline
is matching it), `matched` (`play_id` is the real play: read it with
`GET /v1/plays/{play_id}`), or `failed` (`failure` says why). A
`no_evidence` play stays `sent` with a null `play_id`.
Whether background (ambient) plays are on, until when, and how often each screen plays.

patch.summary: Switch ambient plays on or off
patch.description:
Background (ambient) plays: while on, each simulated screen plays its
campaigns during its site's opening hours, about `plays_per_hour`
times an hour, each with the evidence its simulation profile
describes. Off by default. Switching it on (or sending `ambient: true`
again) runs it for 24 hours from now; it then switches itself off, so
a forgotten sandbox stops making plays.

post.description:
Puts this sandbox back to how it started: everything in it is removed
(sites, screens, devices, campaigns, creatives, plays, events, test
plays) and it is seeded again from its starting point; a copy of your
live setup is taken afresh. Its test keys and webhook endpoints are
kept, so your configuration still works; an endpoint scoped to
particular screens or sites is pointed at the new ones by name. Ambient plays switch off. Typically the first step of a CI run.

Takes a few seconds. `skipped` says what a copy of live left out to
stay inside the sandbox's limits; `endpoint_scope_entries_lost` counts
scope entries whose screen or site no longer exists.

post.summary: Make a simulated screen do something
post.description:
Has a simulated screen's Harvester report an event, exactly as a real
one would, so the real pipeline produces its effects and webhooks:

| type | what the Harvester sends | what follows |
|---|---|---|
| `calibration` | a calibration-complete colour reading | a new baseline; `screen.calibrated` |
| `quality_good` | colour readings matching the baseline | `screen.quality` with every channel `GOOD` |
| `quality_bad` | readings well below the baseline | `screen.quality` with channels `BAD` |
| `screen_off` | the screen switching off | later plays on it read `SCREEN_OFF` |
| `screen_on` | the screen switching on | plays on it are scored normally again |

A quality event on a screen with no baseline calibrates it first (so
`screen.calibrated` comes too). As on a real screen, `screen.quality`
fires at most once per screen per 10 minutes: a second quality event
sooner than that is folded into the next one. Returns at once with a
`test_screen_event` (`status: queued`); it is sent within seconds.

202.description: Accepted — the event is sent in the background.

Location.description: URL of the test screen event to poll.

get.description: `queued` (accepted), `sending` (going out now), `sent` (the Harvester events went out), or `failed` (`failure` says why).

oauth2.description:
Access tokens are opaque, short-lived and
introspected.

scopes.account:read: Read the signed-in user, accessible organisations and entitlements.
scopes.account:write: Create organisations and set the default organisation.
scopes.screens:read: Read screens and screen size ranges.
scopes.screens:write: Create, update and delete screens; assign sites and harvesters; calibrate.
scopes.advertisements:write: Upload, register, update and archive advertisements.
scopes.plays:read: Read plays and their evidence events.
scopes.webhooks:read: Read webhook endpoints and their deliveries.
scopes.webhooks:write: Create, change, delete webhook endpoints, roll their secrets and retry deliveries.
scopes.test_helpers:write: Run simulated plays and control the simulation in an integrator sandbox (test keys only).
scopes.dashboards:write: Create, update and delete the user's dashboards.

secretKey.description:
Organisation secret key, `Authorization: Bearer vojo_live_<secret>`
(or `vojo_test_` for test mode). Hashed at rest, scoped (same
scope names as `oauth2`), with enforced expiry and revocation. Keys have no user: endpoints
marked OAuth-only reject them with 403 `insufficient_scope`.

VojoOrganisation.name: Vojo-Organisation
VojoOrganisation.description:
The organisation this request acts on (org id). **Required for
`oauth2` callers** — a missing header returns 400
`organisation_header_required`; an org the user cannot access (a
membership or an access grant, and granted to this OAuth client)
returns 403 `organisation_access_denied`. **Secret keys** are
bound to one org: the header may be omitted, and if sent it must
match the key's org (else 403). Every query is scoped by the resolved
org, never by an id in the body.

VojoVersion.name: Vojo-Version
VojoVersion.description:
Optional API version pin (a date). Overrides the version pinned on
the secret key / organisation for this request. Echoed in the
`Vojo-Version` response header. Within `/v1` only additive changes
ship, so most callers can omit it.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Client-generated unique key (UUID v4 recommended) making this create
safe to retry. A replay within 24 hours returns the stored response
(with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`). Reusing a key with a different
body returns 409 `idempotency_key_reused`.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size, 1-100. Default 25. A value outside 1-100, or not an integer, is rejected with 400 `invalid_request` (it is not clamped).

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `meta.next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.

Q.name: q
Q.description: Case-insensitive substring search on the resource name (typeahead).

ScopeType.name: scope_type
ScopeType.description: Slice of the fleet to aggregate over. Default `org`.

ScopeId.name: scope_id
ScopeId.description:
Entity id for `scope_type` `site` / `screen` / `campaign` (required
for those, ignored for `org`). Resolved server-side within the org: an
id from another org yields an empty result, never a leak.

VojoVersion.description: The API version (date) this response was rendered with — the request's `Vojo-Version`, else the key/org pin.

RateLimit.description: IETF RateLimit header: remaining quota in the current window, e.g. `"default";r=97;t=42`.

RateLimitPolicy.description: IETF RateLimit-Policy header, e.g. `"default";q=100;w=60`. Portal OAuth clients get a higher tier.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when this response is a stored replay of an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request: invalid JSON, a bad cursor, a missing `Vojo-Organisation` for an OAuth caller, or an unknown `Vojo-Version`.

example.title: Invalid request
example.detail: The request body is not valid JSON.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked credential.

PaymentRequired.description: An entitlement or quota blocks this request. `feature_key`, `limit` and `used` explain which.

example.title: Plan limit reached
example.detail: Your plan allows 3 dashboards; you have 3.

Forbidden.description:
The caller is authenticated but not allowed: missing scope
(`insufficient_scope`), missing permission (`permission_denied`),
a client/installer persona on an operator endpoint
(`operator_access_required`), or no access to the requested org
(`organisation_access_denied`).

example.title: Permission denied
example.detail: You need the networkEdit permission in this organisation.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or belongs to another organisation. Cross-org ids always 404, never 403.

example.title: Not found
example.detail: No screen with that id in this organisation.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with current state (duplicate name, device already paired, idempotency key reuse).

example.title: Duplicate name
example.detail: A screen named "Lobby North" already exists in this organisation.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The declared upload exceeds the per-object maximum (2 GB).

UnprocessableEntity.description: Well-formed request that failed validation. `errors[]` lists each failing field.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded for this principal. Back off for `Retry-After` seconds.

example.title: Too many requests
example.detail: Rate limit of 100 requests per 60 seconds exceeded.

example.title: Internal error
example.detail: An unexpected error occurred. Quote request_id to support.

HarvesterScreenLocation.description: Corner of the screen the harvester sensor is mounted on.

DashboardVisibility.description: `private` = only the owner sees it; `organisation` = every member of the org sees it.

WidgetType.description:
Dashboard widget type. This enum IS the server-side widget catalog
(risk R1): the API validates widget types here, once, and the portal
renders from it. Adding a type is an additive change.

CampaignPlaysTimeframe.description: Timeframe the campaign's expected plays are measured over.

CampaignState.description: Derived from `start_at` / `end_at` relative to now; not stored.

ScopeType.description: Slice of the fleet an aggregate is computed over.

WrapperDeliveryMode.description: `inline` returns the wrapper HTML in the response; `archive` stores it and returns a URL.

Meta.description: Response metadata for single-resource responses. Reserved; currently empty. Clients must ignore unknown members.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Pass it back as `cursor`. `null` when there are no more results.

has_more.description: True when another page exists (equivalent to `next_cursor != null`).

ScopeEcho.description: The scope the aggregate was resolved to, echoed so callers need no extra lookup for a label.

id.description: Entity id for `site` / `screen` / `campaign` scopes; null for `org`.

name.description: Display name of the scoped entity; null for `org`.

ErrorCode.description:
Stable, machine-readable error code (the error-code registry). Branch
on this, never on `title`/`detail`. New codes may be added within v1;
clients must treat an unknown code by its HTTP status.

- `invalid_request`: 400 — malformed JSON, unknown query parameter value or wrong type. - `invalid_cursor`: 400 — the `cursor` is malformed or expired. - `organisation_header_required`: 400 — an OAuth caller omitted `Vojo-Organisation`. - `unsupported_api_version`: 400 — `Vojo-Version` is not a known version date. - `unauthenticated`: 401 — no credential was sent. - `invalid_token`: 401 — the access token or secret key is invalid, expired or revoked. - `entitlement_limit_reached`: 402 — the org's plan does not allow more of this feature (`feature_key`, `limit`, `used`). - `storage_quota_exceeded`: 402 — the upload would exceed the org's storage quota (`limit`, `used`). - `insufficient_scope`: 403 — the token/key lacks the operation's required scope. - `permission_denied`: 403 — the user lacks the required permission in the active org. - `operator_access_required`: 403 — client / installer personas cannot use network endpoints. - `organisation_access_denied`: 403 — the caller has no access to the org in `Vojo-Organisation`, or a secret key's header does not match its org. - `not_found`: 404 — the resource does not exist or belongs to another organisation (never 403, to avoid leaking existence). - `duplicate_name`: 409 — a resource with this name already exists in the org. - `harvester_already_assigned`: 409 — the harvester is already paired to another screen. - `screen_already_paired`: 409 — the screen already has a different device paired. - `no_quality_readings`: 409 — the screen has no quality readings to calibrate from yet. - `idempotency_key_reused`: 409 — the `Idempotency-Key` was used with a different request body. - `idempotency_request_in_progress`: 409 — a request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still being processed. - `screen_busy`: 409 — a test play is already running on this screen; wait for it to be `sent`. - `test_mode_only`: 403 — a test helper was called with a live key; use a sandbox's test key. - `payload_too_large`: 413 — the declared upload size exceeds the per-object maximum (2 GB). - `validation_failed`: 422 — one or more fields failed validation; see `errors[]`. - `upload_not_found`: 422 — the referenced upload does not exist, is not this org's, or was never PUT. - `upload_mismatch`: 422 — the stored object does not match what was declared (size or content type). - `rate_limited`: 429 — too many requests; retry after `Retry-After` seconds. - `internal_error`: 500 — unexpected server failure. Safe to retry idempotent requests.
